text:
mara: quick sync — we should finalize who owns private endpoint lifecycle (creation, cert rotation, decommission) and a simple failover playbook for tenant CP separation.
mara: TL;DR: platform team to own API and lifecycle, infra owns network primitives + NAT mapping, security owns cert ops. open to pushback.
josh: +1 on platform owning API surface. question: who owns emergency IP swap when a relay node flaps?
neal: infra should own the swap, but expose a guarded API to platform so can trigger with audit log. infra owns the ephemeral NAT allocations and static mapping table.
sara: agree but security needs the audit and an allowlist. also prod key rotation must be coordinated — we can't let platform trigger cert changes without a review step.
mara: OK. proposal: 
  - platform: endpoint lifecycle API (create/update/deprecate), rollout policy, canary flags
  - infra: IP assignment, peering configs, NAT/egress mapping, emergency swap API
  - security: cert issuance/rotation orchestration + policy enforcement
  - ops-oncall: runbook & pager escalation
josh: sounds reasonable. we should document an emergency sequence. Draft: 
```
Emergency endpoint failover (brief):
1) infra detects relay node health < 70% or route flaps
2) infra posts to /internal/emergency-swap with reason + incident link
3) platform triggers canary routing to alternate endpoint (30% traffic) for 5m
4) ops verifies smoke (auth, latency, tokens) -> promote to 100%
5) security performs cert recheck and rotation if required
6) close incident and record metrics
```
mara: add metrics: success/failure, P99 delta, auth errors, token-mismatch counts. Ops needs a smoke test script.
neal: I'll attach a quick smoke script prototype: 
```
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" https://tenant-endpoint.example/v1/health
```
sara: also require `--dry-run` mode for the emergency-swap API to preview routing changes and a replayable audit payload.
mara: agreed. add a hard guard: emergency-swap requires 2 approvals if > 5% traffic shift or during business hours.
josh: minor nit: how do we handle DNS propagation? some customers use private DNS in their VPCs. We should prefer a relay-level routing change rather than global DNS.
neal: yep — do not rely on public DNS TTLs. solution: maintain per-tenant endpoint virtual IPs in our relays and update mapping locally. certs pinned to the virtual IP (SAN includes VIP).
sara: that means cert lifecycle ties to VIP ownership — make sure key rotation doesn't require client changes. Use SAN with vip + alt names.
mara: paperwork item: update onboarding docs to state VIPs and routing semantics. Also add a migration path for customers on legacy 'controlplane peering' model — one-time migration job with traffic drain window.
josh: can we add an automated rollback trigger if P99 latency increases > 50% within 10m after swap? make it automatic to reduce toil.
neal: yes — infra can watch metrics and call platform rollback endpoint. should be idempotent.
sara: ops playbook must include a security checklist: key verification, KMS audit, incident record link.
mara: i'll draft the runbook and create a PR to the runbooks repo. goal: ship final doc and API contract by EOD Friday. anyone blocked?
josh: I'll validate DNS/non-DNS customers list and share impact table.
neal: I'll prototype emergency-swap API shape and dry-run response.
sara: I'll write the security gating for cert rotation and approve step.
mara: great — tagging deploy-bot to remind about the canary deploy hooks.
deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: canary hook test at 2026-03-22T14:00Z. :bell: 
mara: thanks — will follow up with PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
